skill.name: to-spec
skill.description: Turns an existing conversation into a tracker-ready product specification without a requirements interview.
skill.summary: Synthesizes current context into a structured spec for issue tracker handoff.
skill.author: mattpocock

content.value_statement: Planning work from a long conversation can lose decisions, constraints, and testing intent. This skill turns existing context into a structured spec and publishes it to the issue tracker.
actual_capabilities: Synthesizes the current conversation into a PRD-style specification.
Explores the repository before writing when code context is needed.
Frames problem statements, solutions, user stories, decisions, tests, scope, and notes.
Uses project vocabulary, ADRs, and architecture context when available.
Publishes the finished spec to the project issue tracker with a ready-for-agent label.
limitations: It does not interview the user or collect new requirements.
It depends on available conversation and repository context.
Issue tracker publishing requires configured tracker access and label vocabulary.
It does not guarantee that generated specs stay current after code changes.

use_cases.title: Feature Planning
use_cases.description: Convert a design discussion into a complete feature specification before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Implementation Handoff
use_cases.description: Capture decisions and testing expectations so another agent or developer can build from a tracker issue.

use_cases.title: Backlog Cleanup
use_cases.description: Turn scattered conversation context into structured issues with scope, user stories, and follow-up notes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Feature Spec
prompt_templates.prompt: Use to-spec to turn this conversation into a specification issue for the feature we discussed.

prompt_templates.title: Document a Bug Fix Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use to-spec to write a tracker-ready spec for this bug fix, including expected behavior, decisions, tests, and out-of-scope items.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Agent Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Use to-spec to publish a spec that another coding agent can implement. Preserve our implementation decisions and testing approach.

prompt_templates.title: Synthesize a Multi-Team Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use to-spec after reviewing the repository context and conversation. Include affected modules, API decisions, data changes, testing decisions, and ownership notes.

output_examples.input: A conversation about adding account balance notifications.
output_examples.output: A tracker issue with a problem statement, solution, user stories, implementation decisions, testing decisions, scope limits, and notes.

output_examples.input: A bug fix discussion with agreed validation behavior.
output_examples.output: A structured spec that captures expected behavior, affected modules, test coverage, and ready-for-agent labeling.

output_examples.input: A planning thread for a cross-team API change.
output_examples.output: A product specification that records API decisions, user impact, ownership notes, testing plans, and out-of-scope work.

best_practices: Provide the full conversation context before invoking the skill.
Make sure issue tracker access and label names are configured before publishing.
Review generated specs for stale assumptions before assigning implementation work.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a requirements interview tool.
Do not publish specs when repository context is incomplete or misleading.
Do not treat the output as approval for unreviewed architecture changes.

faq.question: Does this skill run a requirements interview?
faq.answer: No. It synthesizes existing context and may only confirm the testing approach.

faq.question: Can it create PRDs?
faq.answer: Yes. The output format is a PRD-style feature specification.

faq.question: Will it publish to an issue tracker?
faq.answer: Yes, when tracker access and label vocabulary are available.

faq.question: Does it write code?
faq.answer: No. It creates planning documentation and issue tracker content.

faq.question: Can it use project architecture context?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to inspect the repository and reflect ADRs and project vocabulary.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It is prompt-only and contains no executable files, but tracker permissions still matter.
